content: The text provided appears to be a list of references from various studies, reviews, and articles related to pharmaceutical policies, pricing, and healthcare systems. 1. A study compared oncology treatments with other medical treatments, highlighting the value of health interventions. Published in 2011, it emphasized the need for more comprehensive data to draw conclusions. 2. O'Leary, Usher, and Lynch explored the perspectives of key stakeholders on generic substitution in Ireland. Their findings, published in 2013, revealed insufficient data to fully assess the impact of these policies. 3. Orlewski et al. analyzed the financial impact of Polish human insulin (Gensulin) on public healthcare expenditures between 2001 and 2013. Their 2013 study indicated a lack of sufficient data to evaluate long-term outcomes. 4. Park et al. investigated the differential effects of two pharmaceutical cost-containment policies on outpatient prescription drug expenditures in Korea. Their 2014 study highlighted the complexity of policy impacts but lacked sufficient data for definitive conclusions. 5. Park SE and colleagues examined factors influencing the reimbursement price of new drugs following the introduction of a positive list system in 2012. Their findings underscored the need for more robust data to guide policy decisions. 6. Park Y and collaborators conducted a literature review on factors affecting pricing and competition in the global pharmaceutical market. Their 2016 study identified gaps in data that hinder comprehensive analysis. 7. Patikorn et al. proposed strategies to improve access to high-cost anticancer drugs in ASEAN countries. Their 2018 publication emphasized lessons learned but noted insufficient data for broader application. 8. Petrov and Hubenov introduced formal risk-sharing agreements (RSAs) as a potential solution for sustainable pharmaceutical expenditures in Bulgaria. Their 2015 study highlighted the promise of RSAs but lacked sufficient data for widespread implementation. 9. Puig-Peiró et al. reviewed patient access schemes, flexible pricing, and risk-sharing agreements for medicines. Their 2011 study called for more data to evaluate the effectiveness of these approaches. 10. Putignano et al. assessed the impact of cost-containment policies on the biosimilars market. Their 2014 study revealed insufficient data to fully understand the market dynamics. 11. Qiu et al. examined the inequity of orphan drug prices across Europe. Their 2018 study highlighted disparities but lacked sufficient data for policy recommendations. 12. Raftery analyzed the multiple sclerosis risk-sharing scheme in the UK, describing it as a costly failure in his 2010 publication. The study emphasized the need for better data to evaluate such schemes. 13. Raftery JP explored cost-effectiveness in healthcare, comparing individual drug evaluations by NICE with budget cuts under PPRS. His 2014 study highlighted insufficient data to determine the optimal approach. 14. Relakis et al. conducted a systematic review on the impacts of strict pharmaceutical price controls. Their 2013 study identified methodological challenges and insufficient data for conclusive findings. 15. Rémuzat et al. identified key drivers for the market penetration of biosimilars in Europe. Their 2016 study highlighted the need for more comprehensive data to inform policy decisions. 16. Rong and Sun investigated the impact of pricing policies on short-supplied drugs in Shandong, China. Their 2018 study used an interrupted time series design but noted insufficient data for broader generalization. 17. Samjoo et al. provided insights into the Pan-Canadian Pharmaceutical Alliance's decision not to collectively negotiate drug pricing. Their 2016 study highlighted the complexity of such decisions and the need for more data. 18. Sandhu and Heidenreich discussed the benefits and challenges of performance-linked reimbursement plans for novel drugs, using sacubitril-valsartan as a case study. Their 2018 publication emphasized the need for further data. 19. Saylan et al. analyzed the impact of health policy changes on the unit sales of top-selling pharmaceutical groups in Turkey.
